name: Slate Green
lede: Slate Green is a muted, moderate yellowish green first dated by Ridgway in 1912, one of three slate colors in ColorHub's library alongside Slate-Olive and Slate-Purple.

sections.title: One of three slate colors
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 standard records this hue on plate XVIII, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classes it as a moderate yellowish green, block 150 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates the name to the same year, 1912 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[french-green]], [[american-green]], [[russian-green]] and [[civette-green]], at 2.6, 2.8, 6, 2.8, 3.4 and 4.1 ΔE [1]. Our library also carries at least two other ISCC-NBS names within about 2 units of this exact swatch, a reminder that these old block systems often label the same small patch of color space twice [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to Slate Green in only 85 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.4 percent, as photographed [2]. Inside a painting it plays a midtone more often than a highlight or a shadow, 61 percent of the time [2]. Childe Hassam, Gustav Klimt, Auguste Renoir and Paul Cezanne all use it well above the archive's average rate, with Cezanne's *House of Père Lacroix* (1873) its strongest single match [2].

The earliest dated match is a 1401 painting cataloged only as *King of Hell*, five centuries before Ridgway's plate, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that anyone used this name or pigment that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
